core_obligations: Clause (i): given a local embedding of T_1 into T_2, form the tree P of embeddings of the union of the first n levels of T_1 into those of T_2 for every n, ordered by extension; each level is finite and non-empty, so Konig's lemma yields an infinite branch whose union is an embedding (proof lines 640-644).
Clause (ii): the same argument with embeddings replaced by isomorphisms gives that local isomorphism implies isomorphism, and the converse is immediate from the definitions (proof line 646).

Clause (iii), forward: from elementary equivalence, use the sentence describing the first n levels by naming N points ordered correctly and forcing every other initial segment of n points to lie among them, to conclude that the unions of the first n levels of T_1 and T_2 are isomorphic for every n (proof lines 648-654).

Clause (iii), backward: from local isomorphism, run the back-and-forth game so that the second player answers using the given isomorphisms between unions of finitely many levels, which gives elementary equivalence (proof lines 656-659).
proof_roadmap: Turn local embeddings into a finitely branching tree of finite approximations and apply Konig's lemma (proof lines 640-646).
Compare finite initial segments in both directions: sentences for the forward implication, back-and-forth for the converse (proof lines 648-659).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects three comparisons for omega-trees with finite levels: under the axiom of choice local embeddability coincides with embeddability, under the axiom of choice local isomorphism coincides with isomorphism, and unconditionally local isomorphism coincides with elementary equivalence (statement lines 631-637). The first two clauses turn a local embedding into a genuine one by building the tree of finite approximations and applying Konig's lemma, which is where the axiom of choice enters (proof lines 640-646). The third clause is a two-way comparison of finite initial segments: elementary equivalence is transported into an isomorphism of each pair of finite initial segments by a sentence that pins down the first n levels, and the converse is a back-and-forth argument in which the answer strategy is built from the given local isomorphisms (proof lines 648-659). The content is in the third clause, since it is the only one that does not simply unwrap the definitions with a compactness argument. H2.
